why: The statement asks for classification of ergodic invariant measures for higher-rank diagonalizable actions on homogeneous spaces. Only EKL 2006 settles a restriction of that question (positive-entropy measures on SL(k,R)/SL(k,Z), k≥3): a pre-snapshot case. Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss 2018 is a conditional dichotomy, not a classification of any class, so none. Every in-window item answers a different question: horospherical (unipotent) measures, lattice actions on manifolds, orbit-set dimension, function-field bounded orbits, uniform Littlewood, and namesakes (injectivity radius, Margulis–Platonov, Margulis measures), so all are variant. OpenAI family 015 was the closest call: it proves Haar limits of periodic torus packets using an unidentified measure-rigidity step, which is an equidistribution theorem about limits of periodic orbits, not a classification of A-invariant ergodic measures, so it is variant. Its AI role is coded generated from the lab's blanket statement that the vast majority of catalogue results came from the model; the credit is moot because the events are discarded.
doubts: EKL 2006 is coded unreviewed because the record does not open the journal version (search results say Annals) and checked_by is empty. It is pre-snapshot and a case, so it cannot make the status open_stale either way. The OpenAI AI attribution is a catalogue-wide sentence, not a statement about these particular manuscripts. Coverage of arXiv in the window relies on search results, not direct listings.
